title: N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts hit by breach
summary: N-able has confirmed unauthorised access to a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud environment, after first blaming a worldwide outage on platform configuration and service dependencies. It disabled UI and API access, the dashboard, quarantine, logging and mailbox sync services while it investigates; mail flow and filtering continued. N-able says it has no evidence so far that customer data or mailboxes were accessed, and that the incident is unrelated to the earlier hosted N-central incident.
why: Many Microsoft 365 tenants, especially MSP-managed ones, route mail through Mail Assure or SpamExperts via connectors. While the console is down you cannot release quarantine or change domains, and a filtering vendor with server access sits in your mail path.
todo: Do now: check whether any tenant you manage has inbound/outbound connectors or MX records pointing at Mail Assure/SpamExperts.
Make sure Exchange Online Protection or Defender for Office 365 policies are sane as a fallback, and that connector restrictions (certificate/IP) are in place.
Watch N-able's status page for the final incident report; findings are not verified here.
